baseline_change.title: FWC evidence baseline connected
baseline_change.summary: Three BHP ballot streams and the separate Mining Area C and South Flank agreement application are connected to official records. Worsley’s reported order remains unresolved.

BHP-002.summary: AMWU's BHP Port Operations protected-action-ballot proceeding is connected to an official Commission decision and order.
facts_established: The Commission made the AMWU protected action ballot order on 3 June 2026 in B2026/581.
The order expressly names the AMWU member list as the BHP Port Operations member list.
CiVS was appointed ballot agent and voting was to close on 11 June 2026.
The ballot question asked whether voters authorised stoppages between 30 minutes and 24 hours; the order imposed five working days' notice.
not_established: The Commission documents do not establish that the application was filed on the exact publication date of the 30 May union post.
The order does not establish bargaining strength, operational effect or subsequent use of the authorised action.

BHP-003.summary: The ETU/CEPU ballot campaign is connected to the official CEPU order and published ballot result.
facts_established: The Commission made the CEPU protected action ballot order on 2 June 2026.
CiVS was appointed ballot agent and voting closed on 11 June 2026.
The published result records 102 eligible voters, 89 participants and 89 yes votes to the stoppage question.
not_established: The result does not establish support among employees outside the 102 eligible voters.
The ballot result does not establish that industrial action was subsequently taken or caused operational effects.

BHP-005.summary: The WMWA post's AWU-linked PABO claim is connected to the official AWU decision and order.
facts_established: The Commission record says BHP did not object to the amended AWU application on 19 June 2026.
The Commission made the AWU protected action ballot order on 22 June 2026.
The ballot covered AWU members within the proposed agreement and was to close on 6 July 2026.
The questions covered stoppages and bans on vessel-loading activities.
not_established: The official applicant is the AWU; the Commission record does not use WMWA as a legal applicant name.
The order does not establish bargaining strength, operational effect or workforce-wide support.

BHP-009.summary: The AWU ballot result reported by WMWA is connected to the official declaration, and its denominator is now established.
facts_established: The published declaration records 87 eligible voters and 69 participants, a participation rate of 79.3%.
For each of the two questions, 67 participants voted yes and two voted no, producing 97.1% yes among participants who answered.
The first question covered stoppages between 30 minutes and 24 hours; the second covered bans on vessel-loading activities.
not_established: The 97.1% figure is not 97.1% of all eligible voters and not 97.1% of the broader BHP Port Operations workforce.
The result does not establish participation or support outside AWU members eligible for this ballot.

BHP-017.summary: The PABO decisions establish that compulsory s.448A conciliation was to be programmed, but they do not independently verify the union-reported August meeting dates or bargaining substance.
facts_established: Each PABO decision states that a compulsory s.448A conciliation conference would be programmed or assigned and that bargaining representatives would be required to attend.
not_established: No connected official record independently establishes that the claimed meetings occurred on 4 August or 19–20 August 2026.
No connected official record establishes BHP's offer, the parties' positions at those meetings, or any bargaining movement.

BHP-020.summary: The PABO decisions establish that compulsory s.448A conciliation was to be programmed, but they do not independently verify the union-reported August meeting dates or bargaining substance.
facts_established: Each PABO decision states that a compulsory s.448A conciliation conference would be programmed or assigned and that bargaining representatives would be required to attend.
not_established: No connected official record independently establishes that the claimed meetings occurred on 4 August or 19–20 August 2026.
No connected official record establishes BHP's offer, the parties' positions at those meetings, or any bargaining movement.

BHP-014.summary: The separate Mining Area C and South Flank agreement is connected to the official Agreements in Progress registry and lodged agreement PDF.
facts_established: The frozen 21 August 2026 registry snapshot records AG2026/1877 for the BHP Mining Area C and South Flank Operations Agreement 2026, lodged on 15 July 2026.
At the frozen 21 August snapshot the matter was listed as Member consideration.
The lodged agreement covers employees working exclusively at Mining Area C or South Flank on-site mining operations and excludes Infrastructure and Services teams.
not_established: The pending registry does not establish that the agreement has been approved.
The agreement is adjacent context and is not the proposed BHP Port Operations agreement.

BHP-008.summary: The separate Mining Area C and South Flank agreement is identified, but the union-reported employee vote result is not independently connected.
facts_established: The lodged agreement PDF identifies the separate Mining Area C and South Flank Operations Agreement 2026.
The frozen registry snapshot records its later approval application as AG2026/1877.
not_established: Neither the registry snapshot nor the lodged agreement PDF establishes the reported 58% vote result.
Neither source establishes the reported denominator of approximately 1,800 workers.
The separate agreement does not establish any Port Operations bargaining outcome.

campaign_context.summary: The official AMWU ballot declaration independently records the participation denominator and unanimous yes result among participants.
facts_established: The published declaration records 47 eligible voters and 42 participants, a participation rate of 89.4%.
All 42 participants voted yes and none voted no to the stoppage question.
not_established: The result does not establish support among employees outside the 47 eligible AMWU voters.
The ballot result does not establish that industrial action was subsequently taken or caused operational effects.

campaign_context.summary: The Commission extended the statutory periods for commencing protected action under all three union ballots.
facts_established: The CEPU and AMWU periods were each extended by 30 days, with the extension orders operating from 11 July 2026.
The AWU period was extended by 30 days, with the order operating from 10 August 2026.
BHP advised the Commission it did not object to each extension application.
not_established: Extension of an authorisation period does not establish that protected action occurred, its duration, or any operational effect.

WOR-002.summary: No matching public Commission record was located for the ETU's reported Worsley PABO application under the tested identities.
not_established: The matter number, filing date, employees covered, ballot agent, questions and timetable remain unresolved from official sources.
The negative search result does not prove that no application exists; a recent or differently indexed record may not yet be publicly discoverable.

WOR-003.summary: The ETU's report that the Commission made a Worsley protected action ballot order is not yet connected to a public order or ballot result.
not_established: No official order date, matter number, employee coverage, ballot agent, ballot questions or voting deadline was located.
No Worsley or South32 entry appeared in the Commission's current published ballot-results page at capture time.
The negative search result does not disprove the union report.
